[[Rancho Cucamonga, California]] | former_school(s) = | awards = }} '''Darren Michael Collison''' (born [[August 23]] [[1987]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player. The right-hander is a native of [[Rancho Cucamonga, California]], and is currently playing his senior season for the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]. Collison is widely considered to be one of the top point guard prospects in the 2009 NBA Draft.{{cite web | title= Draft Watch: Getting to the point - ESPN | publisher= ESPN | url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=FordDraftWatch-090115 | accessdate=2009-02-20}} He was awarded the MVP of the [[Maui Invitational Tournament]] in December 2006 and was named the [[Pacific 10 Conference]] Player of the Week on December 4, 2006, and again on February 18, 2007. His parents Dennis and June (Griffith) were both elite track and field athletes for [[Guyana]].{{cite web | title= Player Bio: Darren Collison - Men's Basketball | publisher= UCLA | url=http://uclabruins.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/collison_darren00.html | accessdate=2009-02-20}} Collison grew up as a fan of the [[University of Arizona]], but was not recruited by Arizona, and chose UCLA over [[San Diego State University]]{{cite web | title= Darren Collison - Basketball Recruiting | publisher= Basketball Recruiting | url=http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?Sport=2&pr_key=29729 | accessdate=2009-02-20}} to serve as a backup to [[Jordan Farmar]] in the 2005–06 season. Collison became the starting [[point guard]] the following season. ==Career== ===College career=== [[File:Collison drives to the basket in 2008 Pac-10 Championship game.jpg|thumb|right|Collison at the 2008 Pac-10 Championship game]] Collison is known for both his speed and his defensive ability on both ends of the court.{{fact|date=August 2008}} During the 2006–07 season, he averaged 2.2 steals per game—the most in the [[Pacific 10 Conference]]. He also averaged 5.7 assists (2nd in the Pac 10), as well as a three-point shooting percentage of 44.7 percent.http://uclabruins.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2006-2007/teamcume.html Although Collison was expected by many experts to be a first round pick in the 2007 NBA draft{{fact|date=August 2008}}, he returned to UCLA for his junior year. For the 2007–08 season, he has improved his three-point shooting percentage to 51.7 percent, a school record for a single season.http://www.insidesocal.com/ucla/2008/03/some-stats.html He also
